chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from a man who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A Christian who converted to Islam, then returned to Christianity, and then died — he said: 'His inheritance goes to his Christian children.' And a Muslim who converted to Christianity and then died — he said: 'His inheritance goes to his Muslim children.'
ai.seo_question: Who inherits the estate of an apostate according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the principle of *al-murid bi-ma kana alayhi* (the apostate is treated according to the faith of his children) in Shia jurisprudence. It highlights that inheritance rights are determined by the religious identity of the heirs rather than the deceased's final state, ensuring that Christian children inherit from a Christian apostate and Muslim children from a Muslim apostate. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on familial religious continuity in matters of estate distribution.
